citations.assessment: Avot 2:8 names Shimon among Yohanan’s pupils and explicitly calls him one who fears sin. The next mishnah gives his answer and teaching.
The checked Tosefta gives the marriage report and calls her Gamliel’s daughter’s daughter. Heilprin says daughter.
The direct text says “together with him” and explains that a ḥaver cannot be compelled to handle purity observance for an am ha-aretz. The text does not assign a supervisory role.
The Yerushalmi associates Shimon and the priest with the heavenly announcement that they and their pupils are invited to the third group of the righteous.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: The checked Yerushalmi names Shimon and R. Yosef the priest. The checked Bavli gives R. Yehoshua with R. Yose the priest. Heilprin’s separate priest entry identifies this difference.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: The source explicitly gives the Og, Shimon and Moshe identification and the Bashan letter play as its mystical exposition.
Numbers gives the divine words to Moshe regarding Og. The preceding soul-spark interpretation belongs to Hesed le-Avraham.
The linked notice attributes the location report to Galil Eretz Yisrael and gives competing identifications at the site.

holds.reason: Avot 2 supplies the direct attestation. The separate chapter-five locator was not matched to this name in the checked chapter.

notes.text: The checked Tosefta says Gamliel married his daughter’s daughter to Shimon. Heilprin writes “his daughter.”
The Yerushalmi names Shimon ben Netanel and R. Yosef the priest. The Bavli parallel names R. Yehoshua and R. Yose the priest.
The linked burial notice also records other identifications of the grave.
